thread:
support-sara: heads-up — we've got a spike of 503s to /v1/generate starting ~2026-03-15T17:12Z. multiple customers reporting timeouts and a few error 500s. I see worker containers restarting on hosted-gpu-prod. attaching logs below. :rotating_light:

support-sara: relevant log snippets:
```
[2026-03-15T17:12:03Z] worker-7 PID 2345 SIGSEGV (segfault)
[2026-03-15T17:12:03Z] runtime: total GPU mem 48GB, used 47.9GB -> OOM when allocating 256MB
[2026-03-15T17:12:04Z] containerd: restarting container redwood-runtime-7 (exit code 137)
[2026-03-15T17:12:04Z] proxy: 503 upstream unavailable for request_id=shZk2-345
```

oncall-bot: @channel incident created INC-20260315-0345, priority P1 (customer-facing 503 spike). Paging oncall.

maria: taking lead from runtime. which models impacted and any request ids from customers? any correlation to request size or concurrency?

support-sara: customers reported large-chat sessions (long context), model = redwood-std-13b and redwood-std-70b. sample request id: shZk2-345, another: gF4t9-127. payloads often have long message_history (~8-12k tokens).

ash: looking at node metrics (nv-sku-3.*). GPU mem climbs steadily on worker-7 before crash, no preemptive eviction. docker logs show cuda malloc failures right before OOM. attaching node grafana snapshot: GPU mem percent jumps from 65% -> 98% over ~90s.

leo (support): one customer provided repro curl that reliably triggers a 503 after ~60s of generation on their dataset. sharing curl (redacted api key):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-std-70b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"'"$(python -c "print('A'*90000)")"'"'}],"max_tokens":8192}'
```

maria: that payload looks like it forces huge KV cache growth. there's a known edge-case where the KV allocator doesn't release memory fast enough when sequences are long; could be a leak triggered by recent runtime change (v3.2.1). i'm going to tail logs on runtime and check GC metrics.

infra-jamie: i've cordoned worker-7 and migrated the canary traffic away. creating a temporary routing rule to send traffic for redwood-std-* to quantized variants for safety. doing an emergency scale up of the GPU pool by +2 nodes.

support-sara: thanks. customers affected: Acme, DataSpark, and two smaller teams. acme is escalating via their CSM. i've notified them we're investigating, given ETA ~30m for mitigation.

maria: quick mitigation plan (short term):
- enable fallback to redwood-std-8q for new requests (less RAM)
- reduce max_concurrency per worker to 4
- apply runtime patch v3.2.2 to one canary node -> watch OOM rate

ash: commands i'm running now:
```bash
# update route to quantized fallback for high-memory models
redwood route update --selector hosted --model redwood-std-8q --match-model-prefix redwood-std-
# reduce concurrency on hosted pool
redwood pool update hosted-gpu-prod --max-concurrency 4
```

deploy-bot: deploy started by maria - runtime v3.2.2-hotfix -> canary pool (5% traffic). CI checks passed.

maria: putting a temporary check into the runtime that rejects requests with combined prompt+max_tokens > 20k tokens (soft reject with 400) until we finish the allocator fix. that'll at least prevent the worst cases from creating OOMs.

leo: customer repro verified that routing to redwood-std-8q reduces memory and no 503 observed in 15 runs. warned customer about possible quality drop, they accepted temporary fallback.

infra-jamie: after canary deploy to v3.2.2, canary nodes stayed stable for 20m. OOM events on canary = 0. non-canaried nodes still producing crashes. rolling patch to rest of pool now.

oncall-bot: scheduled action: rollout runtime v3.2.2 -> hosted-gpu-prod at 17:36Z (automated waterfall: 5%->25%->100%). health checks enabled.

support-sara: updating customers: "we've identified a memory leak in the inference runtime triggered by very long contexts; we've deployed a hotfix and are routing you to a lower-memory model as a short-term mitigation. we'll follow up with a postmortem."

product-oliver: please cc me on postmortem. also want an impact summary (customers, duration, tokens lost, estimated revenue risk).

maria: preliminary root cause: regression in KV memory freelist introduced in v3.2.1 — under long-context workloads the freelist fails to recycle large KV pages, causing sustained GPU allocation growth until the driver throws OOM or process segfaults. patch restores correct freelist behavior and adds faster async free path.

ash: note — we also observed one kernel-level GPU driver error on node nv-sku-3-19 (cuda driver 12.2) around same time which probably exacerbated memory behavior; but primary cause is runtime leak. filing an infra bug to pin driver and test.

maria: verification steps used:
1) repro locally with the curl above -> fail on v3.2.1, pass on v3.2.2
2) instrumented runtime metrics (kv_pages, kv_freelist_len) show freelist exhaustion on v3.2.1 and stable on 3.2.2
3) canary -> 0 OOMs for 1 hour under synthetic high-context load

support-sara: customers notified. CSMs logged notes. no new escalations in last 15m. keeping this P1 until full rollout completes.

infra-jamie: rollout to 100% done at 17:52Z. GPU OOM alarms have subsided; 503 rate dropped to baseline.

leo: closing the customer-facing bridge for Acme after they confirm stable. they want the postmortem and timeline.

product-oliver: filing postmortem request — please include timeline, RCA, impact table, mitigation steps, and follow-ups (driver testing, more defensive request-size limits, e2e tests for long context).

maria: follow-ups we own:
- add unit/e2e for large-context KV free path
- telemetry: add a rolling alert on kv_freelist_len/gpu_mem_ratio
- runtime: implement per-request soft cap and clearer 4xx for too-large contexts

support-sara: marking notes for ops-runbook update (how to route to safe model, emergency pool scale commands, rollback steps).

deploy-bot: runtime v3.2.2 rolled out successfully to hosted-gpu-prod at 2026-03-15T17:52:10Z. health: ok.

maria: closing incident in 30m if no regressions. will author postmortem. thanks all. :thumbsup:

support-sara: thanks team. will consolidate comms to customers and close after postmortem posted.
